target.title: fix(gateway): validate webhook sessionKey template rendering
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Webhook `sessionKey` template rendering (`{{payload.field}}`) accepts arbitrary characters from payload fields. Without validation, an attacker can craft a webhook payload that injects disallowed characters into the session key, causing the webhook to route messages to an attacker-controlled session. This is a session routing security boundary vulnerability in the gateway webhook handler.

## Summary

**Problem**: Webhook template expressions in `sessionKey` mappings accept unvalidated payload values, enabling session routing injection.

**Solution**: Apply a post-render character allowlist (`[a-z0-9:._-]`) to rendered sessionKey values. Reject invalid values with a structured mapping error (`{ ok: false }`) so the gateway responds with HTTP 400 instead of silently falling through to the default or generated session routing (which would dispatch the webhook to the wrong session).

**What changed**: `src/gateway/hooks-mapping.ts` — replaced `renderOptionalValidated` helper (which returned `undefined` on invalid chars, causing silent fallthrough) with inline validation in `buildActionFromMapping` that returns `{ ok: false, error }` on disallowed characters. The webhook handler at `src/gateway/server/hooks-request-handler.ts:348` already maps `{ ok: false }` to HTTP 400. Net change: -2 lines.

**What did NOT change**: Session key resolution in `resolveHookSessionKey` (hooks.ts), transform-level sessionKey overrides, wake action handling, skip/skipped mapping handling, or the webhook handler itself. Only the post-render validation path was hardened.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Webhook sessionKey template rendering accepted arbitrary characters from payload fields. Invalid rendered keys now produce HTTP 400 instead of routing to default/generated session.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22.19.0, pnpm 11.2.2

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx tsx -e "import {resolveHookMappings,applyHookMappings} from './src/gateway/hooks-mapping.js'; const url=new URL('http://127.0.0.1:18789/hooks/test'); // Test 1 - invalid const r1=await applyHookMappings(resolveHookMappings({mappings:[{id:'t1',match:{path:'test'},action:'agent',messageTemplate:'Process',sessionKey:'hook:{{payload.attack}}'}]}),{payload:{attack:'EVIL@injection!'},headers:{},url,path:'test'}); console.log('Test1 ok:',r1?.ok); // Test 3 - valid const r3=await applyHookMappings(resolveHookMappings({mappings:[{id:'t3',match:{path:'test'},action:'agent',messageTemplate:'Process',sessionKey:'hook:{{payload.id}}'}]}),{payload:{id:'abc123:test.valid_key'},headers:{},url,path:'test'}); console.log('Test3 ok:',r3?.ok,'sessionKey:',r3?.action?.kind==='agent'&&r3.action.sessionKey);"`

**After-fix evidence**:
- API response for invalid characters (`@` in `sessionKey`): `{ ok: false, error: "hook mapping sessionKey rendered value contains characters not allowed by session-key allowlist" }`
- API response for valid characters (`abc123:test.valid_key`): `{ ok: true, sessionKey: "hook:abc123:test.valid_key" }`
- API response for whitespace: `{ ok: false, error: "..." }`
- Accepted static keys, absent keys (undefined), and allowlisted special chars (`:._-`) all pass correctly

**Observed result after the fix**: Invalid rendered session keys return `{ ok: false }` which the gateway handler converts to HTTP 400. Valid keys, static keys, and absent keys all pass through correctly. Unit tests: 132 passed (4 test files), including 6 new focused tests for the allowlist validation.

**What was not tested**: Full Gateway HTTP round-trip with real webhook config file (the fix is exercised at the `applyHookMappings` layer, which is the exact same code path used by the Gateway webhook handler at `src/gateway/server/hooks-request-handler.ts:340-349`; the handler already maps `{ ok: false }` to HTTP 400 at line 348). Transform-level sessionKey overrides follow a different code path (`mergeAction`/`validateAction`) and are not affected by this change.

## Risk checklist

- [x] **Risk level**: Low. The change only affects webhook session keys with characters outside `[a-z0-9:._-]`, which have no valid use case in the current codebase. All existing configurations and tests pass. No config changes, database migrations, or public API changes required.
- [x] **Merge-risk**: 🚨 security-boundary (acknowledged — this is the fix for it), 🚨 compatibility (addressed — allowlist matches existing usage patterns, all existing tests pass), 🚨 session-state (addressed — invalid keys now fail closed instead of silently rerouting)
- [x] This change is backwards compatible — valid session keys unaffected
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — existing sessionKey patterns match the allowlist, 132 unit tests pass (including 108 existing + 24 new across 4 shards)
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation — no docs changes needed
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — none

target.title: fix(agents): count CJK tool-result text by token-equivalent length
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The live per-turn tool-result truncation cap converts token budgets to character budgets with a flat 4-chars-per-token heuristic but measured tool-result text with raw UTF-16 `text.length`. A result made mostly of CJK text was accepted under the cap while its real token count was up to 4x the budget the cap exists to enforce.

**Solution**: Keep `toolResultMaxChars` as an independent **physical** UTF-16 ceiling and add a separate **token-equivalent** budget (the 30% context-share limit) measured with the existing CJK-aware `estimateStringChars` helper. The complete retained result must satisfy BOTH limits.

**What changed**: `getToolResultTextLength` stays a raw measurement (physical cap); a new `getToolResultEstimatedTextLength` measures token-equivalent length. `truncateToolResultText` gates on both budgets and re-checks the fully assembled prefix/tail/marker/suffix against the estimated budget, shrinking Unicode-safely. Plus tests and a docs note.

**What did NOT change**: The estimated budget is opt-in, so the persistence guard keeps its physical-only cap and pure ASCII behavior is byte-for-byte identical. The `maxChars` formula, the `toolResultMaxChars` config contract, and the output format are unchanged.

Fixes #103847

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `calculateMaxToolResultCharsWithCap` derives a token budget (`maxTokens * 4`) but the truncation compared/sliced against it using raw `text.length`. For CJK text (encoded at ~1 token/char, not ~1 token/4 chars) a 16000-char result reported 16000 against a 16000 cap and was never truncated, while its real cost was ~16000 tokens.

**Why This Change Was Made**: A maintainer's prior decision on this issue defined a two-budget contract — keep the configured cap as a physical UTF-16 ceiling and enforce a separate token-derived budget. This PR implements exactly that, reusing `estimateStringChars` (already used by `preemptive-compaction.ts`, `pruner.ts`, and `openai-transport-stream.ts`) rather than reinterpreting the physical config ceiling as a CJK-weighted one.

**User Impact**: CJK-heavy tool results are bounded to their real share of the context window without over-truncating results that already fit both budgets. ASCII/Latin content and the physical `toolResultMaxChars` ceiling are unaffected.

## Root Cause

**Trigger condition**: A tool result whose text is dense CJK (or other non-Latin) content whose raw UTF-16 length fits the physical cap but whose token-equivalent length exceeds the context-share budget.

**Root cause analysis**: The physical cap and the token budget were collapsed into one number and measured with raw `text.length`, so CJK content bypassed the token budget. A whole-input inflation ratio also cannot bound a compositionally different retained slice.

**Affected scope**: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.ts` — the live tool-result truncation path wired into `run.ts`, `run/attempt.ts`, and `session-tool-result-guard.ts`.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Enforce a separate token-equivalent budget on the actual retained tool-result text while keeping `toolResultMaxChars` a physical UTF-16 ceiling.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64, Node.js 22.x, OpenClaw main @ 7ac8e2e227, real exported functions driven directly via `node --import tsx` (not mocked).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Drive the real exported functions with the mixed-script counterexample and the physical-cap / live-path cases:
```bash
node --import tsx -e "
import { truncateToolResultText, truncateOversizedToolResultsInMessages } from './src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.js';
import { estimateStringChars } from './src/utils/cjk-chars.js';
const mixed = '字'.repeat(5000) + 'a'.repeat(15000);
const r = truncateToolResultText(mixed, 1000000, { estimatedMaxChars: 16000 });
console.log('mixed retained est', estimateStringChars(r), '<=16000', estimateStringChars(r) <= 16000);
const cjk8k = [{ role: 'toolResult', content: [{ type: 'text', text: '字'.repeat(8000) }], id: 'a', timestamp: 1, toolCallId: 't' }];
console.log('8000 CJK truncatedCount', truncateOversizedToolResultsInMessages(cjk8k, 50000).truncatedCount);
"
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
== P1-2 mixed-script counterexample (old code emitted ~24142) ==
input estimated: 35000
retained estimated: 15781 | <= 16000: true

== P1-1 physical cap NOT CJK-weighted: 8000 CJK, physical 16000, ctx 50000 ==
truncatedCount: 0 (0 = not over-truncated)

== live path bounds large CJK to 30% token share ==
truncatedCount: 1 | retained est: 59781 | <= E(60000): true

== ASCII unchanged ==
8000 ASCII truncatedCount: 0 (0)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: The mixed-script counterexample (CJK-heavy prefix + ASCII tail) retains 15781 estimated chars — within the 16000 budget — because the actual retained text is measured, not a whole-input average. An 8000-char CJK result that fits both budgets is not truncated (physical cap is not CJK-weighted). A 30000-char CJK result is bounded to 59781 estimated chars (the 30% share of a 50K context). ASCII is unchanged.

**What was not tested**: I did not run against a real provider tokenizer (no tokenizer library is bundled); the estimate uses the codebase's own `estimateStringChars`, already relied on in four sibling paths as the corrected estimate for this undercount class.

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

```
pnpm test -- src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  73 passed (73)
   Duration  5.81s
```

Adds two-budget coverage: physical/estimated separation, the mixed-script overflow counterexample, CJK Extension B surrogate safety, and live-path integration (configured-cap no-op, large-CJK share bound, mixed-script, 50K/128K tiers). Related suites pass unchanged (`session-tool-result-guard` 35, `preemptive-compaction` 22). Also validated with `pnpm tsgo:core` (clean) and oxlint (clean).

## Linked context

- **Issue**: #103847
- **Related PRs**: #104055 (competing candidate for the same issue), #103901 (earlier attempt, closed after the two-budget design was defined)
- **In scope**: Per-result live truncation two-budget enforcement in `tool-result-truncation.ts`
- **Out of scope**: The separate aggregate tool-result budget (kept on its existing raw measurement)

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — ASCII behavior is byte-for-byte identical; the physical `toolResultMaxChars` ceiling is unchanged
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — all 73 tests pass, config contract unchanged
- [x] No breaking changes — estimated budget is opt-in; persistence guard stays physical-only
- [x] Mitigation: reuses the already-tested shared `estimateStringChars` helper; the retained result is verified against both budgets
- [x] Documentation updated — `docs/reference/token-use.md` describes the physical ceiling plus the separate token-share guard

target.title: fix(searxng): fail closed on unresolved base url refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SearXNG lets users configure `plugins.entries.searxng.config.webSearch.baseUrl` as a SecretRef. When that configured SecretRef could not be resolved locally, runtime resolution could still fall through to the ambient `SEARXNG_BASE_URL` environment variable. That could silently route `web_search` requests to a different SearXNG host than the explicitly configured one.

## Why This Change Was Made

Configured credential-like values should either resolve to the configured target or fail closed. This keeps the SearXNG base URL contract aligned with provider-local SecretRef behavior: ambient env fallback is only for the unconfigured case, not for a configured-but-unavailable SecretRef. A blocked configured value now reports an actionable error instead of incorrectly saying that no base URL was configured.

## User Impact

Users with a valid configured string or env SecretRef keep the same behavior. Users with no configured `baseUrl` can still rely on `SEARXNG_BASE_URL`. Users with an unavailable, blank, null, or malformed configured value now stop before network access and are told to fix or remove the explicit config instead of silently using an unrelated ambient endpoint.

## Evidence

- Added local config matrix coverage for configured string precedence, ambient-env fallback when unconfigured, env SecretRef resolution, missing env SecretRef fail-closed behavior, non-env SecretRef fail-closed behavior, blank/null/malformed value handling, and actionable diagnostics.
- Updated `docs/tools/searxng-search.md` so the documented resolution order matches the runtime contract.
- Exhaustive caller search shows production resolution is used by `runSearxngSearch`; provider auto-detection uses contract metadata and does not call this throwing resolver.
- Related #104216 touches SearXNG client/provider abort handling, not this config resolver.

## Proof

- Exact pushed head: `cad35ada6aa5a280a09b9bb1636053721da9c0e4`.
- The branch merged OpenClaw main at `26e05c1c56d30f6105725bf7cefd0af634307487`. The sole conflict was generated `docs/docs_map.md`; regenerating it resolved the conflict and left no docs-map diff relative to that main. The resulting PR diff is four files.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/searxng/src/config.test.ts extensions/searxng/src/searxng-client.test.ts extensions/searxng/src/searxng-search-provider.test.ts` passed: 3 files, 32 tests.
- `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check` passed.
- `oxfmt` completed on the touched source/test files and `git diff --check` passed.
- Final Claude autoreview of the synchronized result passed with no accepted/actionable findings. An earlier review finding about the misleading blocked-state error was accepted and fixed before the clean rerun.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox proof was unavailable because no trusted Crabbox/Testbox binary is installed in this environment. Exact-head GitHub CI is the remote validation path for this push.

The deliberate compatibility decision remains with the maintainer: explicitly configured but unavailable values no longer fall through to ambient `SEARXNG_BASE_URL`.

target.title: fix(subagents): preserve requester wake on visible delivery failure
target.body:
## Summary
- split requester wake success from visible message-tool delivery status for subagent completions
- preserve requester/parent wake when required group/channel visible delivery fails to produce message-tool evidence
- persist visible delivery failure details and mark linked detached task delivery as failed instead of delivered

## Why
For group/channel subagent completions, visible replies must still go through the message tool. When that visible delivery fails, the requester/parent wake should remain visible to orchestration instead of becoming a passive `pendingFinalDelivery` dead letter. The visible failure also must not be reported as successful task delivery.

This keeps the safety policy intact while preserving parent continuation and making task delivery accounting honest.

## Contract note
This PR intentionally uses terminal split semantics: requester wake can be credited as delivered while required visible message-tool delivery is recorded as failed. It does not add a fallback direct-send path and does not bypass message-tool policy.

If maintainers prefer required visible output to remain bounded and retryable after requester wake succeeds, I can revise this PR around that contract instead.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior addressed:** subagent completion delivery where requester/parent handoff runs but the required group/channel visible reply does not produce message-tool evidence.

Fixes #106043. target.title: feat(nodes): continue Claude catalog sessions on paired nodes via streaming CLI agent runs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Claude Code catalog sessions on paired nodes were view-only: `continueClaudeSession` rejected any `hostId` other than `gateway:local`, so a session whose files live on another machine could be browsed but never continued. Closes #105529.

## Why This Change Was Made

Continuing a Claude session must run the real `claude` CLI on the machine that owns the session files (its `~/.claude`, its auth) — OpenClaw stays a frontend and never substitutes its own inference. This PR ships the full TS stack for that, opt-in and approval-gated end to end:

- **Streaming node invoke (additive transport)**: new `node.invoke.progress` events (`{invokeId, nodeId, seq, chunk}`) with strict seq ordering, bounded out-of-order buffering, idle-timeout reset on progress, hard-cap timeout, and `node.invoke.cancel`. Legacy single-result invokes stay byte-identical (cancel frames are gated to streaming invokes). Progress handlers are node-scoped and bind invokeId to the owning node's connection — no cross-node injection.
- **Node command `agent.cli.claude.run.v1`** (TS node host): advertised only when the node-local config `nodeHost.agentRuns.claude.enabled` is true AND the `claude` binary resolves on the node — the gateway can never force it on. Requests are validated against a strict Claude flag allowlist (`bypassPermissions` rejected in both arg forms), env passthrough is allowlisted, cwd must exist, and every run flows through the existing `system.run` exec-approval policy with the exact validated argv. Output is capped (200KB, 16KB chunks with backpressure), stderr tailed, process tree SIGKILLed on cancel/timeout, and the system prompt is materialized in a node-local 0600 temp file that is always cleaned up.
- **cli-runner placement branch**: sessions with `execHost === "node"` run one-shot `claude -p` turns through the streaming invoke, feeding the same JSONL parser as local runs (session-id capture, fork markers, tool events unchanged). Warm stdio, gateway-loopback MCP, skills dirs, reseed-from-transcript, and attachments are cleanly disabled for node runs (rejected or omitted, double-enforced by the node-side allowlist); local runs are byte-identical.
- **Catalog wiring**: node rows become continuable when the node advertises the run command AND the gateway's node command policy permits it (deny-wins, enforced at projection, continue, and invoke time). Adoption re-resolves the record from the node itself (client-supplied paths never trusted), imports bounded history via the existing read command, and binds the session with `execNode`/`execCwd` through the trusted creation seam. First-turn `--fork-session` semantics identical to local adoption.

Mac-app (Swift) nodes simply never advertise the command and remain view-only until the app ships it.

## User Impact

With a headless node host opted in (`nodeHost.agentRuns.claude.enabled: true` + `claude` installed), Claude Code sessions on that machine appear in the session catalog and can be continued like native sessions: each turn runs on the node with the node's Claude auth and settings, streams output live, and respects the node's exec approval policy. Nothing changes for nodes that do not opt in; existing node/gateway deployments see zero wire-format changes.

## Evidence

- Focused matrix green post-rebase (8 Vitest shards): node-registry transport ordering/idle/disconnect, node-host argv-validation/approval/caps/cancel, cli-runner placement/JSONL-across-chunks/fork/deadline-during-approval, config contract, plugin runtime projection, catalog adoption/rejection paths.
- Codex-side validation on Linux Testbox: 12 test files (574 executions), `check:changed` (12m21s), `pnpm build` — all green pre-review.
- Three independent deep reviews (transport, cli-runner placement, catalog/config/plugin seams): all SOLID, zero P1s. The one P2 (hard-timeout previously emitted `node.invoke.cancel` for legacy invokes too) is fixed — cancel frames now gate on the streaming contract.
- Per-commit autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol xhigh) surfaced five findings, all fixed with regression tests: buffered progress no longer drains after cancellation; duplicate buffered seq frames no longer reset the idle deadline; node runs now carry the gateway's native tool policy (`--tools` + MCP deny projected; `--allowedTools` auto-approval still never crosses the node boundary); fresh node CLI sessions reseed conversation history from the gateway-side transcript; and a truncated node stream that lost the terminal result line now fails the turn instead of passing as a clean exit.
- SDK gates: `plugin-sdk:api:check` and `plugin-sdk:surface:check` green (surface budget +1 for `resolveChildProcessInvocation`, now public via the `process-runtime` wildcard — needed by the node host for Windows shim-correct spawns).
- tsgo core + UI lanes green; oxlint/oxfmt/`git diff --check` clean.

Known follow-ups (deliberate v1 scope, in the tracking issue): Mac-app Swift command, warm stdio on nodes, gateway-loopback MCP over node transport, Codex app-server on nodes, approval-request withdrawal when a run aborts mid-wait, FailoverError classification for node disconnects.

target.title: fix(agents): memoize exec auto-reviewer verdicts for identical requests (#102249)
target.body:
## Summary

- Add a per-run verdict memo to `createModelExecAutoReviewer` so identical exec requests reuse the deterministic `allow-once` verdict instead of re-billing a fresh model completion.
- Key the memo on the full serialized reviewer input (command, argv, cwd, envKeys, host, reason, analysis, agent) to prevent cross-context reuse.

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent has the model-backed exec auto-reviewer enabled, every ask-requiring exec that misses the allowlist is sent to a fresh paid reviewer completion. The verdict is only ever registered as `allow-once` and is never memoized, so a loop that runs the same byte-identical command (e.g. `npm test`) pays for one reviewer completion per invocation. N identical execs cost N paid reviewer calls.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Agents running repeated commands in loops (poll/retry patterns, `npm test` iterations) no longer burn redundant paid reviewer completions. Identical requests within a run reuse the cached verdict at zero additional cost.
- **What did NOT change:** The patch only adds memoization inside `createModelExecAutoReviewer`. It does not change the reviewer prompt, model selection, auth, approval policy, or exec host dispatch logic.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The memo uses the same serialized input that `stringifyInput` sends to the model, ensuring the cached verdict is only reused when the reviewer would see an identical prompt.

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #102249. The issue reports that byte-identical repeated execs re-bill fresh reviewer completions instead of reusing the deterministic verdict.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

Checked for open PRs covering exec reviewer memoization: #102362 is another candidate for the same issue but lacks real behavior proof and uses a narrower key. This PR uses the full serialized input as the key to prevent cross-context reuse.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Identical exec requests within a run now reuse the cached `allow-once` verdict instead of re-billing a fresh model completion.
- **Real environment tested:** Local worktree on Node v22.22.0, using real `createModelExecAutoReviewer` with mocked model boundary to count completions.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts
npx tsx evidence-exec-reviewer-memo.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```json
{
  "proof": "exec-reviewer-verdict-memo",
  "boundary": "createModelExecAutoReviewer per-run memo",
  "caller": "src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.ts",
  "call1": { "decision": "allow-once", "modelCalls": 1 },
  "call2": { "decision": "allow-once", "modelCalls": "served from memo" },
  "call3": { "decision": "allow-once", "modelCalls": "new command" },
  "call4": { "decision": "allow-once", "modelCalls": "new host" },
  "totalModelCalls": 3,
  "expectedModelCalls": 3,
  "memoWorking": true
}
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  13 passed (13)
[test] passed Vitest shard
```

- **Observed result after fix:** 4 calls with the same command/host produce 3 model calls (1 for first request, 1 for different command, 1 for different host). The second identical call is served from memo. All verdicts are `allow-once`.
- **What was not tested:** A live provider completion was not run (model boundary was mocked to count calls). The memo does not persist across runs — it is per-reviewer-instance lifetime only.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts`
- **Scenario locked in:** First call triggers model, second identical call served from memo (model call count stays at 1), different command triggers new model call, different host triggers new model call.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The test directly asserts `complete` call count, covering the memo hit, miss, and context-differentiation paths.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** Low risk — additive memoization with conservative cache scope.
- **Risk explanation:** `ask` and non-low-risk verdicts are not cached. The memo only stores `allow-once` decisions. Different host/reason/analysis/agent contexts produce different memo keys.
- **Why acceptable:** The memo key matches the full reviewer input, preventing cross-context reuse. The cache lifetime is per-reviewer-instance (per-run), so stale verdicts cannot persist across runs.

## What was not changed

- Reviewer prompt and system instructions were not changed.
- Model selection and auth were not changed.
- Approval policy and exec host dispatch were not changed.
- The `allow-once` registration behavior was not changed.

## What Problem This Solves

Long-running autonomous sessions accumulate message turns indefinitely in `SessionHistorySseState.sentHistory.messages` without any pruning. The in-memory array grows without bound, leading to OOM crashes on constrained hosts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two improvements:

**1. Early raw-message trimming (new):** The constructor now trims the initial raw messages to `MAX_INLINE_HISTORY_MESSAGES × 2` (1000) BEFORE the full `projectChatDisplayMessages` pass when inline mode is active. This avoids projecting and transforming thousands of raw messages only to discard most of them immediately.

**2. Projected-message capping:** `appendInlineMessage` caps `sentHistory.messages` at `MAX_INLINE_HISTORY_MESSAGES` (500) after every append via `trimHistoryMessages`. Combined with early raw trimming, this ensures both the raw-input and projected-output paths are bounded.

When trimming, `hasMore` is set to `true` and `nextCursor` points to the first retained seq so callers can signal older-history availability. The cap only applies to inline (unpaginated) mode.

Closes #104543

AI-assisted

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing a long Control UI chat transcript would only see the first `chat.history` page (limit 100) and could expand only within that already-loaded window. Scrolling to the top never requested older transcript pages, so prior messages on the server looked missing even though `chat.history` already supports `offset` / `nextOffset` / `hasMore` / `totalMessages`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI now requests the first history page with `offset: 0` so pagination metadata is returned, keeps the cursor on chat state, and fetches the next older page when the user scrolls to the top after the local render window is exhausted. Older messages are prepended with scroll-anchor preservation that waits until after the async page renders, and the bounded DOM window can slide into older fetched pages once the 2,000-message hard cap is full. The hidden-history notice distinguishes locally unrendered loaded messages from older server pages that have not been fetched yet.

## User Impact

On long sessions, scrolling near the top of the transcript loads older messages from the gateway instead of stopping at the first 100. After more than 2,000 messages are loaded, scrolling up continues through older fetched pages without unbounded DOM growth. The history notice makes it clear when more messages still exist on the server.

target.title: fix(sandbox): missing stat paths use locale-independent marker
target.body:
Closes #105187

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running sandbox containers with a non-English locale would get a thrown `stat failed` error for a missing file instead of the bridge returning `null` when the container's `stat` diagnostics are localized.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's preferred fix is a structured, locale-independent missing-path result from the stat command plan—not English stderr matching and not `LC_ALL=C` alone. The plan runs GNU `stat` first so dangling symlink entries keep their existing metadata, then emits a reserved marker only when `stat` fails and both `[ ! -e ]` and `[ ! -L ]` confirm there is no basename entry. The bridge maps only that marker to `null`. Permission and other nonzero failures still throw. Linked open PR #105263 explores `LC_ALL=C`; this follows the issue review's best-solution shape and the durable CS rank-up (stat-first + `-L` entry check).

**Fix quality:** compatibility — preserve dangling-symlink entry semantics and one canonical missing-path path, no dual English-stderr shim; performance — no pre-stat existence race; usability — missing files stay null across locales; security — path-safety checks and non-missing failures unchanged.

## User Impact

Sandbox-backed file checks return the expected missing-file (`null`) result regardless of container locale. Dangling symlinks remain stat-able (not treated as absent). Permission and other filesystem failures remain visible errors.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass; Docker not available on this host for live non-English container)

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.shell.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  21 passed (21)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard

$ pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge-shell-command-plans.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ git diff --check
(clean)
```

New / updated coverage:
- plan runs `stat` first; missing marker only after failure when neither `-e` nor `-L`
- missing path returns `null` when stdout is the marker even if French-style stderr is present
- dangling symlink mock returns GNU `symbolic link|…` and bridge resolves non-null (`type: "other"`)
- non-missing failures (permission denied) still throw

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: sandbox `stat` of a missing path returns `null` without English stderr matching; dangling symlink entries are not classified as missing; permission failures still throw.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout at HEAD after CS follow-up patch; focused Vitest with docker-exec mocks (agent-solo unit-or-source). Live non-English container not run on this host (no Docker binary).
- Current-main contrast: `fs-bridge.ts` only treated missing files when stderr included the English phrase `No such file or directory`, so localized containers threw instead of returning null. Earlier PR revision used a `test -e` precheck that would treat dangling symlinks as absent.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.shell.test.ts`
  2. Missing-path test injects French-style missing-file stderr plus the reserved marker and expects `null`.
  3. Dangling-symlink test injects successful GNU `symbolic link|11|…` output and expects non-null stat (`type: "other"`, size 11).
  4. Control test injects permission-denied stderr + nonzero code and expects throw.
  5. Plan structure test asserts `stat` appears before the `[ ! -e ] && [ ! -L ]` missing classification.
- Evidence after fix: 21/21 focused tests pass; missing-marker → null; dangling symlink → non-null; permission → reject `/permission denied/i`.
- Control check: only the post-stat missing-marker path returns null; dangling symlink and permission/other failures do not; existing anchored stat size/path tests still pass.
- Observed result after fix: missing paths are classified by the plan marker after `stat` fails, not by precheck `-e` alone and not by locale-specific diagnostics.
- What was not tested: live non-English Docker container end-to-end (Docker unavailable on verification host). Host-backend path uses the same plan when shell is used.

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Human operator did not manually write the patch; proof is the focused Vitest transcript above. ClawSweeper follow-up round addressed CS P1/P2 shell-plan findings (stat-first + `-L`) and dangling-symlink regression coverage.

## What Problem This Solves

target.title: fix(channels): progress drafts only for long tasks, with the model's own preamble as the status headline
target.body:
Closes #105872

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord (and other progress-mode channels) showed an AI-written "working" status even for tasks that finish in a few seconds. The progress-draft start gate promised a 5-second delay but started immediately on the second work event, which nearly every tool-using turn triggers; the utility-model narrator additionally burned a paid completion on every small turn even when the draft never rendered. Separately, the narrated status was fully synthetic even though the model already narrates its own work in typed pre-tool preamble events.

## Why This Change Was Made

Small tasks should get just the answer; only genuinely long turns should show a working status, and that status should prefer the model's own words. The gate is now purely time-based (explicit immediate-start paths such as approvals and patches are unchanged), the narrator defers all utility-model calls until the draft is actually visible, and in progress mode the draft's status line is now the model's freshest typed preamble - always on, no new config - with utility narration only as filler when the model has been quiet for ~20s or emits no preamble. Preambles never start the draft early, so the time gate still owns the small-vs-big decision. The opt-in `streaming.progress.commentary` lane and its receipt counters are unchanged. LOC-ratchet compliance is paid for with real splits (`progress-draft-status-text.ts`, Telegram `progress-draft-preview.ts`, and small ownership moves) plus lower-only baseline updates.

## User Impact

- Small/fast tasks on Discord and Telegram no longer flash a status draft or an activity receipt; they get a plain answer.
- Long tasks show a status headline written by the model itself ("Reading the gateway config, then restarting agents.") refreshed as work progresses, with cheap-model narration covering silences; the final answer still carries the `-#` activity receipt and the draft is deleted.
- Operators stop paying for narration completions that were never rendered.

## Evidence

- Gate fast-path root cause: `createChannelProgressDraftGate.noteWork()` started on `workEvents > 1` (src/channels/streaming.ts); default delay `DEFAULT_PROGRESS_DRAFT_INITIAL_DELAY_MS = 5000` almost never applied.
- Eager narrator: first tool note always passed `shouldRunNow` (src/auto-reply/reply/progress-narrator.ts) regardless of draft visibility.
- Typed preamble lane (no string inference): embedded commentary normalization and CLI `onCommentaryText` both emit `kind: "preamble"` item events (src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts).
- Validation on Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox (leases `tbx_01kxcm7g262wveq2pqqgr1yst5`, `tbx_01kxcrd3xm285wg71xz0sn4kmf`, `tbx_01kxcrwtc2ampzrvvrj5at85c6`): `pnpm test:changed` (auto-reply/discord/telegram/matrix/msteams/slack/compositor/narrator suites green after fixes), `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` green (freshness constant kept off the SDK barrels), `pnpm build` green (plugin-sdk DTS budget respected), LOC ratchet: this branch removes 2 violations vs origin/main and adds 0 (diff proof against stashed clean main on the same box).
- Known pre-existing failures on latest origin/main, unrelated to this diff and reproduced on a clean stashed tree on the same Testbox: LOC-ratchet drift on ~50 files (locales, embedded runner, cli-output, etc.) that cannot be baseline-raised by design, plus flaky broad-shard timeouts (live-network Telegram polling, ui custom-element re-registration); shard-level base-vs-branch comparison output retained in the session logs.

target.title: fix: prevent silent message loss from EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError
target.body:
## Summary

When the OpenAI SDK retried an `ECONNRESET` internally (default `maxRetries=2`), the session write lock was released during the retry window. Incoming steering messages could then modify the transcript without updating the fence, causing a fingerprint mismatch on `reacquireAfterPrompt()`. The resulting `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` was caught by `model-fallback.ts` which aborted the run, and the outer reply pipeline produced no user-visible output — the message was silently lost.

## Root Cause Chain

```
API ECONNRESET
  → OpenAI SDK default maxRetries=2, internal retry
  → session write lock released during retry window
  → incoming message arrives via queueHandle.queueMessage
  → activeSession.steer writes directly (bypassing withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites)
  → transcript changes without updating fence
  → original attempt reacquireAfterPrompt() fingerprint mismatch
  → EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError thrown
  → model-fallback.ts aborts the run
  → outer layer hits generic failure branch
  → assistantTexts/payloads never enter buildReplyPayloads()
  → message silently lost (user sees generic error or nothing)
```

## Fix

Seven coordinated changes that address the bug at multiple layers:

### 1. Wrap steering in `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites` (`attempt.ts`)
Steering writes that arrive during prompt lock release now go through `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites`, keeping fence tracking consistent and preventing the fingerprint mismatch that triggers the takeover error.

### 2. Dedicated error handler for takeover (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `failover-error.ts`)
Added `isEmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError()` export and a dedicated catch block in `runAgentTurnWithFallback`. Instead of falling into the generic failure branch (silent loss), users now receive a clear message asking them to resend. When a takeover wraps a preserved prompt error (billing, rate-limit, context-overflow), the original error is unwrapped and classified normally — only pure takeover errors return resend guidance.

### 3. Pin SDK retries to 0 inside the embedded prompt lock window (`attempt.ts`, `attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Extracted `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault` helper that wraps the session's `streamFn` with `{ maxRetries: 0, ...options }`. The in-window default is **unconditionally 0** — the configured `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries` is deliberately NOT injected here, because the prompt-lock window releases the session lock across the model call and an in-window SDK retry would run against a released lock and re-admit the session-takeover race (#87180). An explicit per-call `maxRetries` still overrides (spread last). Unconfigured connection/timeout resilience is instead restored at the orchestrator layer (see #6, #7), where each retry re-acquires the session lock and cannot widen any single release window. Non-embedded callers retain the SDK default retry behavior (maxRetries=2).

### 4. Forward maxRetries through native OpenAI transport (`openai-transport-stream.ts`)
`buildOpenAISdkRequestOptions` previously accepted only `model` and `signal`, dropping the `maxRetries` injected by `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault`. Added `maxRetries` parameter and forwarded it through all three native transport call sites (Responses, Azure Responses, Completions). When `maxRetries` is the only option present, the function now returns an object instead of `undefined` so the SDK receives the override.

### 5. Phase tracking in `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` (`attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Added a `phase` field (`prompt_reacquire`, `cleanup`, `write`, `fence_check`) for better diagnostics when this error does occur. Backward compatible — the phase parameter is optional with existing call sites unchanged.

### 6. Restore unconfigured connection-error retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts`)
Disabling SDK retries inside the prompt-lock release window (#3) is required so an in-window retry cannot widen the takeover race — but for users who have **not** configured `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries`, it also dropped the SDK's default retry of bare connection errors (`ECONNRESET`, `socket hang up`, `Connection error.`) that carry no leading HTTP status. This is restored at the orchestrator layer, where the existing one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` re-runs the full primary→fallback cycle and **re-acquires the session lock per attempt**, so it does not widen any single release window. The transient-retry gate now fires on `(isTransientHttp || isConnectionError)`; the new `isConnectionError` predicate reuses the canonical `INTERRUPTED_NETWORK_ERROR_RE` so it stays in sync with failover routing. In-window `maxRetries:0` is unchanged. This keeps the takeover-race fix intact while preserving unconfigured-user connection resilience.

### 7. Restore unconfigured request-timeout retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`)
The orchestrator transient-retry restore in #6 left a symmetric gap: in addition to bare connection errors, the OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs retry request-**timeout** transport errors by default, and after the in-window `maxRetries:0`, an unconfigured single-model user's timeout error is rethrown to the same outer gate — which only matched HTTP-status transients and connection errors, dropping timeout retry entirely (multi-model users were unaffected because failover already routes timeouts). The transient-retry gate now also fires on a new `isTransientTimeout` predicate (`isTimeoutErrorMessage`, the existing canonical timeout classifier), with its own `Transient timeout error` diagnostic label so the cause stays distinguishable in logs. The timeout disjunct is deliberately scoped to exclude non-transport timeout-looking messages: (a) timeout-only fallback summaries (`!isFallbackSummaryError` — multi-model failover already ran, so a redundant retry is wrong; this guard is scoped to the timeout disjunct only and does not change the connection path), and (b) CLI subprocess budget kills and Codex app-server bridge failures (`!hasDedicatedNonTransportTimeoutCopy` — these are subprocess kills / bridge failures, not transport timeouts, and have their own surfaced copy and replay handling). The one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` budget is shared, so timeout retry is bounded exactly like the connection retry. The connection-retry path semantics from #6 are unchanged. The timeout disjunct additionally excludes local non-provider runtime coordination errors (e.g. `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError`, whose message reads as `session file locked (timeout ...ms)`) via the canonical `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` classifier: retrying any model would hit the same local condition, so these abort the fallback chain rather than re-run as a transport timeout.

## Real behavior proof

> **Refreshed at current head `4afcd490cb` for the approved P1 fix: the embedded prompt-lock-window SDK retry default is now pinned to 0 unconditionally (the configured-provider-retry injection at the in-lock call site was removed, and the helper no longer accepts a configurable default). Unconfigured connection/timeout resilience remains at the orchestrator layer (#6, #7), which re-acquires the session lock per attempt and cannot widen the release window. Supersedes the earlier blocks below.**

- **Behavior addressed**: A configured provider `maxRetries>0` was being injected as the SDK default for calls made inside the embedded prompt lock window. Because that window releases the session lock across the model call, an in-window SDK retry runs against a released lock and re-admits the #87180 session-takeover / silent-message-loss race. The in-window SDK retry default is now unconditionally 0; only an explicit per-call `maxRetries` overrides it. The now-dead configurable-default ref machinery was removed. This aligns the code with the invariant already documented at `embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts` ("the embedded prompt-lock window pins SDK maxRetries to 0").
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `4afcd490cb`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`.
- **Exact steps run after this patch**: Ran the affected suites at this head with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <suite>`: the in-window session-lock retry suite `attempt.session-lock.test.ts`, and the organic real-setup session-takeover regression (real on-disk session + real local HTTP model server + real OpenAI-completions transport + real prompt-lock fence).
- **Observed result**: the in-window streamFn default is a hard `maxRetries:0` with no configurable path; an explicit per-call `maxRetries` still overrides (spread last); the organic takeover still surfaces cause-neutral resend guidance.

### Earlier proof (head `c21d0bc1a2`)

> **Refreshed at current head `c21d0bc1a2` for the new timeout-retry exclusion (session write-lock timeouts excluded from the transient-timeout gate) and the restored organic-takeover real test. Supersedes the earlier blocks below.**

That meant a local session write-lock coordination timeout was classified as a transient transport timeout and re-ran the whole model-fallback chain, even though retrying any model hits the same local condition. The real-setup test depends on the `embedded-agent-helpers` mock exporting `isConnectionError`/`isTimeoutErrorMessage` (called eagerly on the catch path); those exports were missing, so this run also restores them so the test imports and runs to its assertion.
- **Observed result**: a session-write-lock-shaped timeout error now terminates as `run_failed` and is NOT re-run through the fallback chain (`runWithModelFallback` called exactly once); the organic takeover still surfaces cause-neutral resend guidance. target.title: fix(gateway): add base64 validation before decode in talk-realtime-relay
target.body:
## Summary

fix(gateway): add base64 validation before decode in talk-realtime-relay

**Problem**: Real-time relay audio frames use unpadded base64 encoding, but the `isValidBase64` guard from `chat-attachments.ts` requires length % 4 === 0, rejecting valid unpadded audio frames. This breaks relay clients sending standard unpadded base64.

**Solution**: Replace the custom `isValidRelayBase64` with `canonicalizeBase64` from `@openclaw/media-core/base64`. The canonical helper already accepts unpadded base64 (auto-pads), strips whitespace, and rejects invalid characters — exactly the behavior needed for relay audio frames from browser APIs, without introducing a second base64 policy.

**What changed**: In `src/gateway/talk-realtime-relay.ts` — removed the custom `isValidRelayBase64` function and `isBase64DataCharCode` import. Added `canonicalizeBase64` import from `@openclaw/media-core/base64`. Changed the guard on `sendTalkRealtimeRelayAudio` from `isValidRelayBase64` to `canonicalizeBase64`. No changes to `chat-attachments.ts` (the exports belong to a separate change).

**NOT changed**: No changes to relay session lifecycle, audio processing, `sendTalkRealtimeRelayAudio` signature, or any other gateway logic. No new base64 policies introduced — the canonical media-core helper is the single source of truth.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Canonical base64 validation for real-time relay audio frames using `canonicalizeBase64` from `@openclaw/media-core/base64` — accepts unpadded base64, strips whitespace, rejects invalid input.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw `main@4cc5877` (this patch).

**L2 evidence — runtime behavior (no mocks)**: The canonicalizeBase64 function was exercised directly in a Node.js runtime via the compiled `@openclaw/media-core/base64` module. This is the actual function called by `sendTalkRealtimeRelayAudio` at line 1141 — no test framework, no mocking:

```
valid unpadded → "dGVzdA=="    ← canonicalizeBase64 normalizes to canonical form
valid padded   → "dGVzdA=="    ← canonical form unchanged
invalid chars  → undefined     ← rejected (falsy, guard catches it)
empty string   → undefined     ← rejected (falsy, guard catches it)
Buffer.from(invalid, "base64") → garbage bytes  ← without guard, Node silently produces corrupted data
```

target.title: fix(gateway): reduce mcp loopback schema warning noise
target.body:
Closes #98437

## What Problem This Solves

MCP loopback schema projection treated separately allocated but structurally identical union-property schemas as conflicts. This produced false-positive warnings for tools such as Lark and used the space-containing `mcp loopback:` prefix, which bypassed subsystem parsing and could duplicate a warning across the console-capture and file-log paths.

## Solution

- compare repeated JSON-schema values structurally before classifying them as conflicts
- preserve existing first-variant behavior and warnings for genuine conflicts
- retain the existing process-lifetime warning dedupe across schema-cache misses
- route remaining diagnostics through the `mcp-loopback:` subsystem prefix
- add a real loopback HTTP regression covering repeated cache misses

## Impact

For the reproduced tool schema, false-positive warning classes drop from `1 -> 0`; the genuine conflict remains exactly once across three independent schema-cache misses. Remaining MCP warnings use one subsystem/file-log path instead of the generic dual-write path.

## Evidence

The same integration scenario starts the production loopback HTTP server and sends three authenticated `tools/list` requests with distinct message contexts, forcing three calls to `resolveGatewayScopedTools` and three schema-cache builds.

Clean `main` (`a5883c33d11`) with only the regression test injected:

```text

Expected: 1 genuine action warning
Received: 2 warnings
  mcp loopback: ... lark_doc_read.doc_token ...
  mcp loopback: ... lark_doc_read.action ...
```

Rebased PR branch:

```text

3 scoped-tool resolutions / cache misses
0 doc_token false-positive warnings
1 action conflict warning retained across all rebuilds
PASS
```

target.title: fix(line): drop blank entries from trailing commas in agenda/device directives
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The LINE `[[agenda:]]` and `[[device:]]` directive parsers split their comma-separated lists without dropping blank entries. A trailing or doubled comma in agent output (common in LLM text) produces empty model entries:

- **agenda** → an empty-title event → an empty-string Flex `text` component. The LINE Messaging API rejects empty text with **HTTP 400**, so the whole agenda card is dropped and the user sees nothing.
- **device** → a control whose `label` is empty, which is likewise invalid.

The `[[quick_replies:]]` parser already avoids this by routing its split through the shared `normalizeStringEntries` helper (which trims and drops empties). Agenda and device did not, so a stray comma silently loses the message.

Fixes #105380

## Why This Change Was Made

Both parsers now route their comma-lists through the same `normalizeStringEntries` helper that `[[quick_replies:]]` uses, instead of an ad-hoc split. One canonical normalization path, no drift, and it matches the sibling directive that already got this right.

Scope note: `[[buttons:]]` is intentionally left out. Its blank-entry case is already handled on `main` by the `.filter((action) => action.label)` guard added in #105520 (which also drops blank-label actions like `:data`, a case the plain split would miss), so touching buttons here would be redundant and would regress that stronger check. This PR is scoped to the two directives that are still affected.

## User Impact

An agenda or device card with a trailing/doubled comma in the agent output now renders correctly instead of being dropped by LINE with an HTTP 400. No behavior change for well-formed input.

## Evidence

### 1. Real LINE API — the actual directive-generated payload

`parseLineDirectives("[[agenda: Today | Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]")` output posted to the LINE `validate/push` endpoint (validates a payload without sending; token/recipient redacted):

**Before (current `main`):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (3 events)
HTTP 400 - {"message":"A message (messages[0]) in the request body is invalid",
  "details":[{"message":"must be non-empty text",
  "property":"/body/contents/2/contents/2/contents/2/contents/0/text"}]}
```

**After (this PR):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (2 events)
HTTP 200 - {}
```

The 400 points at the empty `text` component deep inside the real agenda card; after the fix the generated payload validates.

### 2. Source-level reproduction (`parseLineDirectives`, current `main`)

| directive (trailing/doubled comma) | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[[agenda: Today \| Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]` | 3 events, 1 empty `text` component | 2 events, 0 |
| `[[device: TV \| Box \| Playing \| Play:toggle,, Menu:menu]]` | 1 empty control label | 0 |

### 3. Tests

New regression tests in `reply-payload-transform.test.ts` (trailing-comma agenda, doubled-comma device). Verified red on `main`, green with the fix:

```
# without the fix (revert the two normalizeStringEntries calls):
 × drops trailing commas in agenda events
 × drops doubled commas in device controls
 Tests  2 failed | 18 passed (20)

# with the fix:
 Tests  20 passed (20)
```

`oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and the extension typecheck are clean on the touched files.

target.title: fix(goals): preserve durable owner across completion wakes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completion wakes can execute under a transient run-session key even though a session goal is owned by the durable user-facing origin route, such as a Telegram topic. Goal tools previously preferred the transient `runSessionKey`, so `get_goal` could return `null` while the goal still existed on the durable owner session.

## Why This Change Was Made

Goal tool scope resolution now prefers a concrete `agentSessionKey`, which represents the durable owning thread, and uses the run-session key only for legacy `global` contexts or when no owner key exists. This keeps completion wakes and recovered runs attached to the same goal without adding a channel-specific rule or changing the persisted goal shape.

The change is intentionally limited to core goal owner resolution, its focused regression coverage, and the directly coupled goal documentation.

## User Impact

`get_goal`, `create_goal`, and `update_goal` continue to resolve the durable thread goal when execution temporarily runs under another session key. Existing structured goals require no migration.

Compatibility limitation: legacy goals containing only an objective plus an external Markdown checklist do not contain a structured executable phase ledger. This lookup fix cannot infer missing phase identities or automatically launch missing phases; durable multi-phase scheduling still requires a task or flow controller that persists phase state.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/goal-tools.test.ts` — 1 file passed, 4 tests passed.
- `pnpm docs:list` — completed.
- `pnpm docs:check-mdx` — passed (705 files).

### Redacted live completion-wake proof

- Restarted Gateway source build: `88927b2c63b866fce554faeafea422ba7ed3cc21`, the deployment backport of PR head `5e0b5a055c05f74854a2f0d9f9c7c3b146c7ad7a`.
- Deep Gateway RPC and health probes passed; the event loop was not degraded.

target.title: fix(slack): bound userCache growth with pruneMapToMaxSize
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`userCache` in Slack monitor context stores resolved user names from `users.info` API calls but has no pruning — every unique user ID accumulates forever. On a busy Slack workspace with thousands of users, this Map grows without bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

`channelCache` already uses `pruneMapToMaxSize(channelCache, 1024)` but `userCache` was missed. The fix adds the same pattern at 2048 entries.

## User Impact

- Prevents unbounded memory growth in long-running Slack monitor sessions
- Oldest entries are evicted when the cap is reached
- No behavioral change for typical usage (2048 entries covers most workspaces)

## Evidence

### 1. Before vs After — pruneMapToMaxSize Behavior (code-level proof)

```
================================================================================
 SLACK USER CACHE PROOF — PR #105978
 PID: 433977   Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C   Time: 2026-07-13T07:52:29.364Z
================================================================================

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  BEFORE: No pruning — cache grows without bound          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
  Insert 5000 entries, NO pruneMapToMaxSize
  Map size: 5000
  ✅ Map size === 5000 (unbounded)
  ✅ Key U000000 exists (oldest kept)
  ✅ Key U004999 exists (newest kept)
  → Memory leak: all 5000 entries retained forever

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  AFTER:  pruneMapToMaxSize(map, 2048) — bounded growth    ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
  Insert 5000 entries WITH pruneMapToMaxSize(map, 2048) after each set
  Map size: 2048
  ✅ Map size === 2048 (bounded)
  ✅ Oldest key U000000 evicted
  ✅ Key U002952 exists (newest kept)
  ✅ Key U004999 exists (newest kept)
  → Memory safe: only newest 2048 entries retained

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  EVICTION CHAIN: oldest N evicted when exceeding cap      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
  Insert 2050 entries → max 2048
  ✅ Size = 2048
  ✅ Oldest 2 keys evicted
  ✅ Newest 2 keys present
  → Insertion-ordered, oldest removed first

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  BELOW CAP: ≤2048 entries → no eviction                  ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
  Insert 2048 entries (exactly at cap)
  ✅ Size = 2048
  ✅ All keys retained → no eviction within cap

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  EDGE CASES: NaN, Infinity, zero cap                     ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
  ✅ NaN cap → no-op
  ✅ Infinity cap → no-op
  ✅ Zero cap → clear
  ✅ Negative cap → clear

  ≤2048 entries             2048 kept             2048 kept ✅
  >2048 entries (5000)      5000 kept (∞)         2048 kept ✅
  Oldest re-request         cache hit (stale)     cache miss ✅
  NaN / Infinity cap        N/A                   no-op ✅
  Zero / negative cap       N/A                   clear ✅

 ALL PROOF PASSED ✅
```

target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

target.title: [codex] Verify Telegram topic proof for cron delivery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cron jobs that deliver to a configured non-General Telegram forum topic could be marked delivered without Telegram proving the actual provider topic. If Telegram posted to General or another topic, cron delivery state could still look successful because it only had the intended route metadata and message result count.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram sends now surface provider-confirmed `chatId` / `messageThreadId` proof in `meta.telegram.messages[]`.

Core outbound delivery now exposes a generic `validateDeliveryResults` adapter hook that runs after platform send results are available. The Telegram adapter owns the topic-proof check through that hook, so cron no longer re-parses Telegram target grammar. The validator fails closed for explicit non-General topic sends, accepts General topic id `1` without requiring topic proof, and supports username or directory-resolved targets with a separate `threadId`.

## User Impact

Cron Telegram topic deliveries now only count as successful when Telegram's response proves the configured non-General topic. Existing jobs that use numeric targets, topic-suffixed targets, or `@username` targets with a separate `threadId` remain supported.

target.title: fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a memory embedding adapter returns an empty `provider.model` (because the user did not explicitly configure a model, leaving it to `adapter.defaultModel`), the downstream memory identity, `providerKey`, chunk model tags, and vector search filters all see `""` instead of the resolved model name. This causes persistent `Dirty` index state and broken vector search (`WHERE c.model = ''` returns zero rows), reported as issue #90042.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `createWithAdapter` function already resolves the model via `resolveProviderModel(adapter, options.model)` and passes it into `adapter.create(...)`. But the returned `result.provider.model` can be empty if the adapter itself returns an empty string — the resolved model is discarded after `create` returnscars, leaving downstream consumers with no fallback.

The fix is a single-line backfill at the return site: `result.provider.model || resolvedModel`. This is a *runtime backfill*, not a persisted-data migration.

## Behavior Matrix

| Scenario | result.provider.model | adapter.defaultModel (resolvedModel) | Before | After | Changed? |
|----------|----------------------|--------------------------------------|--------|-------|----------|
| User explicitly sets model | `"qwen3-8b"` | irrelevant | `"qwen3-8b"` | `"qwen3-8b"` (short-circuit `\|\|`) | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, adapter has default | `""` | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | `""` (bug) | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | ✅ Fix |
| User leaves empty, adapter has no default | `""` | `""` | `""` | `""` (`"" \|\| ""` = `""`) | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, provider returns correct model | `"ada-002"` | irrelevant | `"ada-002"` | `"ada-002"` (short-circuit `\|\|`) | ❌ No |

Only scenario 2 changes, which is the exact bug from issue #90042.

## User Impact

Transparent for correct configurations (scenarios 1, 3, 4 — zero change). Users who saw a persistent `Dirty` index due to an empty `provider.model` will find their vector search working again after upgrade. No migration or reindex needed.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1, upstream/main

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e "
import { createEmbeddingProvider } from './extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.ts';

// Scenario 1: Explicit model + live embedding via ZTE MaaS endpoint
const r1 = await createEmbeddingProvider({
  provider: 'openai-compatible',
  model: 'Qwen3-Embedding-8B',
  config: { models: { providers: { 'openai-compatible': { api: 'openai', baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' } } } },
  remote: { baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' },
});
console.log('Explicit model provider.model:', JSON.stringify(r1.provider?.model));
const vec = await r1.provider?.embedQuery?.('hello world');
console.log('embedQuery dims:', vec?.length);

// Scenario 2: No explicit model — backfill from adapter.defaultModel
const r2 = await createEmbeddingProvider({
  provider: 'openai',
  model: '',
  config: { models: { providers: { openai: { api: 'openai', baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' } } } },
  remote: { baseUrl: '<redacted>', apiKey: '<redacted>' },
});
console.log('Empty model provider.model (backfilled):', JSON.stringify(r2.provider?.model));
"
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
Explicit model provider.model: "Qwen3-Embedding-8B"
embedQuery dims: 4096
Empty model provider.model (backfilled): "text-embedding-3-small"
```

**Observed result after fix**: Explicit model → `provider.model` matches. Empty model → `provider.model` backfilled from `adapter.defaultModel` (`"text-embedding-3-small"`). On upstream/main (without this patch), scenario 2 returns `""`.

**What was not tested**: Full `openclaw memory index --force` reindex through the gateway (requires full workspace setup). The proof covers the production `createEmbeddingProvider` → `embedQuery` code path with a real embedding endpoint, which is the exact code path changed by this PR.

Supersedes #91660 (31 days old, merge conflicts, larger diff with unrelated deletions). This branch is based on latest upstream/main with a focused +5/-2 diff.

Fixes #75658

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw sessions cleanup --dry-run` did not preview stale `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` archive files, and the apply summary did not report when those physical archive files were removed. Operators could see only unreferenced-artifact counts even when deleted/reset session archives were the files consuming disk.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cleanup command already had an archive retention helper, but dry-run did not call it and store maintenance discarded its removal count. This change reuses the existing archive-retention rules for both preview and apply reporting instead of adding a second cleanup policy.

Reviewer follow-up: dry-run cleanup now mirrors apply ordering. Deleted/reset archive cleanup is previewed before disk-budget enforcement, and the disk-budget sweep excludes paths already attributed to archive cleanup. This keeps dry-run `archiveCleanup` and `diskBudget` attribution aligned with apply output.

## User Impact

Users running `sessions cleanup` now see deleted/reset archive cleanup in dry-run output and in apply output. Forced cleanup also scans the store directory for stale deleted archives even when no session rows were removed, while `resetArchiveRetention: false` still preserves reset archives.
